title: General Performance Guarantee for Human Torque Estimation-Based Task-Agnostic Assistive Exoskeleton Control
abstract: arXiv:2609.39558v1 Announce Type: cross  Abstract: Accurate human torque estimation is crucial for enabling task-agnostic control in robotic exoskeleton systems. However, estimation errors may cause mismatches between the robot assistance and the human intention, degrading controllability and task performance. In this paper, we address this issue by formally defining matched assistance as scenarios in which the robot positively contributes to human movement. Based on this definition, we develop a theoretical framework to design the robot's desired interaction torque that guarantees a lower bound on the matched assistance probability. Importantly, the proposed guarantee holds over the entire torque distribution, including unseen data beyond the training tasks. This provides our method with strong reliability and generalization, both of which are critical for effective exoskeleton control. translated_title: 基于人体力矩估计的任务无关辅助外骨骼控制的通用性能保证
translated_abstract: 准确的人体力矩估计对于实现机器人外骨骼系统中的任务无关控制至关重要。然而，估计误差可能导致机器人辅助与人体意图之间的不匹配，从而降低可控性和任务性能。本文通过正式定义“匹配辅助”（即机器人对人体运动产生积极贡献的场景）来解决这一问题。基于该定义，我们开发了一个理论框架，用于设计机器人的期望交互力矩，从而保证匹配辅助概率的下界。重要的是，所提出的保证在整个力矩分布上均成立，包括训练任务之外的未见数据。这为我们的方法提供了强大的可靠性和泛化能力，而这两者对于有效的外骨骼控制都至关重要。所提出的策略已在ABLE上肢外骨骼上实现，并在多任务（评估中验证了其有效性）。
tldr: 本文提出了一个理论框架，可为基于人体力矩估计的任务无关外骨骼控制设计期望交互力矩，并保证匹配辅助概率的下界，且该保证覆盖包括训练任务之外未见数据在内的整个力矩分布。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a theoretical framework that designs the robot's desired interaction torque to guarantee a lower bound on the matched assistance probability for task-agnostic exoskeleton control based on human torque estimation, with the guarantee holding over the entire torque distribution including unseen data beyond training tasks.
